designs.title: Pisa
designs.why: Clean, printable one-ink line art: strokes are a consistent ~4-5px (about 0.7mm at print size), there are no hairlines or halftones to clog the screen, and it reverses well to white on black. The stamp idea reads straight away: perforated edge, the '3.97°' lean as the stamp value, a postmark that breaks the frame, and wavy cancel lines. Crops show the tower's arcades, the belfry and the diamond inlays at the base are drawn carefully, and the type is crisp. What holds it back from $50: every line is the same weight and the tower is open outline only, so from 3 m it reads as a light, grey, even line drawing without much punch. The arcade tiers also get dense, close to filling in on a heavy plastisol or white underbase on black.
designs.fix: Add weight contrast: make the shaded side of the tower (or the stamp's background field) a solid or bold-hatched mass, and thicken the outer silhouette and the frame relative to the inner arcade lines. That gives the print a strong dark-light read from a distance, and it opens up the dense arcade gaps so they print safely.
